text:
- [LEXP.7.19] **`Bytes` and whole `Json` values admit equality and no
  ordering.**

  - The engine **must** answer `==` and `!=` on two `Bytes` operands by
    content: they are equal iff they have the same length and the same octet
    at every position ([LSTR.4.1]).
  - The engine **must** answer `==` and `!=` on two `Json` operands by the
    deep structural equality [LFAC.2.5.1] applies to a `Json` slot, so a
    comparison and a no-op reassertion agree on whether two values are the
    same.
  - The compiler **must** refuse `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` when either operand
    is a `Bytes` value or a whole `Json` value, with
    `DS_VALIDATE_UNORDERED_TYPE`, at the operator. In a comparison chain each
    step is judged on its own two operands.

  A whole `Json` value is a `Json` slot read without a path. A path into a
  `Json` slot reads a leaf whose type is known only at run time, and its
  comparison is [LEXP.7.12.1]'s. A `null` operand propagates ([LNUL.4.1]). The
  refusal holds whatever the other operand's type. Equality between a `Bytes`
  or whole `Json` operand and an operand of another type is outside this
  clause.

idris.name: iret_7_5__cmp_json
idris.note: `==` and `!=` on two `Json` operands by [LFAC.2.5.1]'s deep structural equality; a `null` operand propagates ([LNUL.4.1]); an operand of another kind is a TypeError, a trap here. An ordering on two `Json` values answers as a trap here, which the compiler refuses before any runtime sees it; the `Bytes` bullet is outside the fragment.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__json_eq
idris.note: The deep structural equality the engine answers `==` and `!=` on two `Json` operands by -- one definition for the comparison and the no-op reassertion, so the two agree.
